messages:
arjun: quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC thread — I sketched a lightweight proposal for incremental shard coherence + backpressure so warmup doesn't stall PGs.
maya: nice. can you paste the sketch here? quick bullets ok.
samir: high level concerns: 1) safe on-disk format (safetensors), 2) deterministic atomic swaps for shard versions, 3) backpressure signals from runtime -> weight loader to avoid OOMs.
arjun: agreed. sketch:

- metadata-first manifests: shard manifest contains offsets, fanout, checksum, and an optional 'warm_priority' score. always load manifest before any bytes.
- weight source abstraction: unify urls/tarball/s3/safetensors/zip under WeightSource API that exposes async get_manifest(shard_id) and stream_chunk(range).
- warmup planner: given manifest + workload hint, schedule non-blocking prefetch with priorities and deadlines. warmup should be advisory — not required for correctness.
- coherence contract: we atomically switch active shard pointer (model -> shard_version) only after the runtime confirms KV cache primed or after fallback policy triggers. no partial write visible.
- backpressure: if memory pressure or too many concurrent prefetches, loader returns a short-circuit signal. runtime responds by queuing requests or falling back to smaller model variant.

code sketch:
```
interface WeightSource {
  async get_manifest(shard_id) -> Manifest
  async stream_chunk(shard_id, offset, length) -> byte_stream
}

// WarmupPlanner picks ranges and parallelism based on memory_budget
WarmupPlanner.plan(manifest, budget) -> [prefetch_ops]
```

ellen: sounds good. a few nitpicks: 1) atomic swap requires deterministic on-device layout to avoid pointer chase during swap. 2) what about safetensors shards that aren't splittable (single-file packed)? we need range-read or pack-index.
arjun: idea: always generate a small index companion file (shard.idx) next to safetensors shard with chunk boundaries. loader falls back to full-file if no index. index-first keeps streaming warmup possible.
maya: +1 on shard.idx. also recommend a lightweight validation step: quick checksum of first N headers to detect corrupt uploads early.
samir: backpressure shape: two dimensions — bandwidth (io) and memory (gpu/host). prefer to expose both to caller. suggest signals: ACCEPT / THROTTLE / REJECT with optional retry-after ms and 'fallback_hint' e.g., model:small.
devops-bot: CI note: index generation step will require small packaging change in the model-publish pipeline. ticket: INF-4872 created.
arjun: tradeoffs:
- eager warmup (fast cold latency) vs cost: more IO and memory.
- blocking warmup simplifies correctness (no fallback) but hurts tail latency and availability.
- index companion increases artifact count but enables zero-copy range reads and fine-grained scheduling.

sam: interface boundaries question: should WarmupPlanner live in runtime or in loader service? i vote runtime-owned: it has realtime signals (cache hits, memory usage) and better admission control.
ellen: runtime-owned but keep planning logic pluggable. for private deployments the loader might be on a different host, so planner should be able to emit plan + runtime provide feedback loop.
arjun: ops-wise: we need metrics: per-shard prefetch ops, throttled_count, swap_failures, avg_warm_time. add traces for plan -> fetch -> swap.
samir: can we reuse existing KV cache readiness bit? i.e., mark shard ready once top-K layers loaded per manifest hint. otherwise default to full warm.
maya: good call. Manifest field: { min_ready_layers: int, priority: float, indexes: [offsets] }
arjun: questions for RFC follow-up:
1) agree metadata-first + shard.idx companion mandatory for new artifacts but allow legacy fallback?
2) define exact backpressure signals API (ACCEPT/THROTTLE/REJECT + retry-after + fallback_hint).
3) ownership: WarmupPlanner in runtime, loader implements WeightSource and exposes manifest+range streams.
4) atomic swap semantics (two-phase swap with validation hook).

ellen: vote: metadata-first + idx optional but preferred. runtime planner owned. backpressure API as sketched. two-phase atomic swap.
sam: volunteer to draft wire API and proto for backpressure signals.

arjun: thanks — I'll open a follow-up RFC (shard-coherence-backpressure) with the sketches + perf numbers. target: perf probe on a handful of models to pick defaults for min_ready_layers and parallel prefetchers.
maya: I'll sync with publishing infra on shard.idx generation and add INF-4872 to their backlog.
sam: I'll start proto and a tiny mock loader to simulate THROTTLE cases.
devops-bot: Created RFC draft: rfc-1769-shard-coherence-backpressure.md, link: https://go/infra/rfc/1769
arjun: great. closing note: keep runtime fallbacks explicit (log fallback_reason) — opaque silent fallbacks are hard to debug.

— end of thread
